answer: First, each node commits an epoch-locked state root: it allocates a dedicated 2 GB RAM array and hashes it with Blake3 under a per-node salt, producing a unique digest that cannot be copied across identities. Verifiers then cross-check these roots along a shared vine of prior epochs, so one node's committed array must stay consistent with every neighbor's history. A Karst-style porous check follows: random 64 KB slices are requested mid-epoch, and any mismatch in the digest becomes a tamper signal that revokes the identity's voting weight and slashes its 500-token bond.
